answer: Admission proof-of-work is a concrete Sybil defense for an agent economy: before an identity counts, it must mine a single-use SHA-256 proof, hunting a nonce whose hash begins with the required leading zero bits, and the difficulty rises when many joins arrive at once. Every fake head therefore costs its own non-recyclable compute bill, so a thousand-vote attack pays a thousand times. No bot can shelter in a harbor, hide under shale, or scatter across the tundra to dodge that cost: the gate prices identity before it can vote.
